scenes.visual: Title card 'Where the Marsh Grass Goes' over a tidal salt marsh of tall grass at low tide. COLOUR MAP, same in both films and matching the lesson's EnergyBudgetLadder interactive: GREEN box = producers (plants); PURPLE pipe = production passed up to the next level; BROWN door and BROWN soil box = detritus (dead matter: uneaten production and feces); GREY wavy arrows rising = heat from respiration; consumer boxes are pale outlines with a cartoon animal inside. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text, in kJ m^-2 yr^-1 unless labelled. Boxes, pipes and cartoons are schematic and labelled 'schematic, made-up budget'. In this film the GREEN box is smooth cordgrass.

scenes.tts: In the made-up budget, decomposers respired far more than the grazers and predators. Most plant production was never eaten by a grazer at all.
scenes.visual: A quick recap of the made-up budget: GREEN producer box, herbivore box, a thin PURPLE pipe, wide BROWN streams into the BROWN soil box, tall GREY heat arrows rising from the BROWN box and short ones from the animal boxes. Tag: 'made-up budget'.
scenes.narration: In the made-up budget, decomposers respired far more than the grazers and predators. Most plant production was never eaten by a grazer at all.

scenes.tts: Was that just a quirk of invented numbers? In a real ecosystem, where does the plants' production actually end up each year?
scenes.visual: The made-up tag peels off and the boxes fade to outlines. A question mark hovers over the BROWN door. The scene dissolves to a real coastline.
scenes.narration: Was that just a quirk of invented numbers? In a real ecosystem, where does the plants' production actually end up each year?

scenes.tts: John Teal asked this on the coast of Georgia. He built an energy budget for a salt marsh, and published it in nineteen sixty-two.
scenes.caption: John Teal asked this on the coast of Georgia. He built an energy budget for a salt marsh, and published it in 1962.
scenes.visual: A map of the southeastern United States zooms to the Georgia coast. Name card: 'John Teal, Ecology, 1962'. Tidal creeks wind through a flat green marsh.
scenes.narration: John Teal asked this on the coast of Georgia. He built an energy budget for a salt marsh, and published it in 1962.

scenes.tts: One grass dominates these marshes, smooth cordgrass. It grows in the tidal mud and makes a great deal of plant matter each year.
scenes.caption: One grass dominates these marshes, smooth cordgrass (Spartina alterniflora). It grows in the tidal mud and makes a great deal of plant matter each year.
scenes.visual: Tall cordgrass blades rise from grey-brown mud as tide water slides in and out. The grass gathers into the GREEN producer box, labelled 'smooth cordgrass, Spartina alterniflora'.
scenes.narration: One grass dominates these marshes, smooth cordgrass (Spartina alterniflora). It grows in the tidal mud and makes a great deal of plant matter each year.

scenes.tts: A grazing-chain picture of ecology predicts the obvious route. Grass feeds the herbivores, and then the herbivores feed the predators.
scenes.visual: A schematic arrow chain draws itself: GREEN grass box → insect grazer cartoon → spider cartoon, linked by a fat PURPLE pipe. Label 'grazing-chain prediction (schematic)'.
scenes.narration: A grazing-chain picture of ecology predicts the obvious route. Grass feeds the herbivores, and then the herbivores feed the predators.

scenes.tts: Teal did not assume the route. He assembled the budget from measurements of the grass and the algae on the mud. It also drew on measurements of the animals and bacteria living there.
scenes.visual: Measurement icons pop onto the marsh one by one: a clipped grass quadrat, a magnified patch of algae on the mud surface, small crabs, snails and insects, and a microscope circle of bacteria. Each icon drops into a box on the budget diagram.
scenes.narration: Teal did not assume the route. He assembled the budget from measurements of the grass and the algae on the mud. It also drew on measurements of the animals and bacteria living there.

scenes.tts: Insects and other animals graze on the living grass. Will they take most of its production, or only a small part?
scenes.visual: Insect cartoons perch on green blades, chewing. Two option tags: 'most of it' and 'a small part'. The PURPLE pipe from the GREEN box to the grazers flickers between fat and thin.
scenes.narration: Insects and other animals graze on the living grass. Will they take most of its production, or only a small part?

scenes.visual: Hold the frame; a 5-second countdown; on-screen 'Predict: how much of the grass do grazers take?'

scenes.tts: Only a small part. In Teal's budget, the purple pipe to the grazers was thin. The grazing chain was a side channel.
scenes.visual: The 'a small part' tag lights. The PURPLE pipe to the grazers settles thin. The fat schematic pipe from scene s05 fades out, replaced by this thin one. Label 'grazers: a small part of production'. No numbers shown.
scenes.narration: Only a small part. In Teal's budget, the purple pipe to the grazers was thin. The grazing chain was a side channel.

scenes.tts: Much of the grass died instead, and broke into fragments. Bacteria used those fragments, and so did animals that feed on detritus.
scenes.visual: Season fast-forward: grass blades yellow, fall and break into fragments that drift onto the mud and wash through the BROWN door into the BROWN box. Inside the BROWN box, bacteria cartoons and detritus-feeding snails and crabs gather around the fragments. A wide BROWN stream dominates the diagram.
scenes.narration: Much of the grass died instead, and broke into fragments. Bacteria used those fragments, and so did animals that feed on detritus.

scenes.tts: Those detritus feeders are themselves eaten. So detritus is not a dead end for animals. It is a second route into the food web.
scenes.visual: A generic predator cartoon (labelled 'schematic consumer') picks snail and crab cartoons out of the BROWN box. A PURPLE pipe now rises out of the BROWN box as well, labelled 'detrital route (schematic)'.
scenes.narration: Those detritus feeders are themselves eaten. So detritus is not a dead end for animals. It is a second route into the food web.

scenes.tts: Every organism on this route respires. Each one releases heat through a grey door. The energy never returns to the grass.
scenes.visual: GREY wavy arrows rise from the bacteria, the snails, the crabs and the schematic consumer, the animals on this route. A dashed arrow from the BROWN box back to the GREEN grass box is crossed out, labelled 'energy: no return'.
scenes.narration: Every organism on this route respires. Each one releases heat through a grey door. The energy never returns to the grass.

scenes.tts: Only matter cycles. Nutrients return to the grass through its roots. Carbon returns as carbon dioxide, which the leaves fix again. The energy comes from fresh sunlight.
scenes.visual: Small dots labelled 'nutrients' travel from the BROWN box through the mud into the grass roots. Separate dots labelled 'carbon' rise from the decomposers into the air as 'CO2' and enter the grass blades as the leaves photosynthesize; a few carbon dots stay buried in the mud and a few drift out with the tide. Fresh sunlight arrows enter the GREEN box from above, labelled 'energy in'.
scenes.narration: Only matter cycles. Nutrients return to the grass through its roots. Carbon returns as carbon dioxide, which the leaves fix again. The energy comes from fresh sunlight.

scenes.tts: Teal's budget also left a remainder. After the respiration of bacteria and animals, about forty-five percent of net production was left over.
scenes.caption: Teal's budget also left a remainder. After the respiration of bacteria and animals, about 45% of net production was left over.
scenes.visual: A ledger bar for the marsh's net production. GREY segments slide off for 'respiration of bacteria and animals'. What remains is outlined with a dashed border and tagged 'remainder: about 45% of net production'.
scenes.narration: Teal's budget also left a remainder. After the respiration of bacteria and animals, about 45% of net production was left over.

scenes.tts: He took it as available to leave the marsh with the tides. But it was a remainder, not a measured export.
scenes.visual: A dashed arrow carries the dashed segment out a tidal creek toward open water, labelled 'available to leave with the tides?'. A stamp lands across the arrow: 'remainder, not a measured export'.
scenes.narration: He took it as available to leave the marsh with the tides. But it was a remainder, not a measured export.

scenes.tts: Even so, the study changed the picture. With others' work on decomposing marsh grass, it moved detritus from a footnote to the centre of coastal budgets.
scenes.visual: A textbook page with a small footnote marked 'detritus'. The footnote slides up and grows into the central, widest box of a coastal budget diagram, BROWN, with GREEN, PURPLE and GREY around it.
scenes.narration: Even so, the study changed the picture. With others' work on decomposing marsh grass, it moved detritus from a footnote to the centre of coastal budgets.

scenes.tts: So keep the brown door in every budget. In this marsh, most grass production went that way rather than to grazers, and respiration released its energy as heat.
scenes.visual: Return to the full marsh diagram: thin PURPLE pipe to grazers, wide BROWN stream to detritus, GREY heat arrows rising from every box. The BROWN door is outlined and labelled 'keep it in the budget'.
scenes.narration: So keep the brown door in every budget. In this marsh, most grass production went that way rather than to grazers, and respiration released its energy as heat.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot standing in marsh grass. Take-home line: 'Detritus belongs in every energy budget; its energy also leaves as heat.'
